I'm 75 this year, been farming these same 6 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. Only had a few years of school, but I know my land better than any book. My son and his wife work in the factory over in the county town, so it's mostly me and my old lady doing the day-to-day work. They come back for harvest and when things get busy. Six mouths to feed, so I can't be throwing money around.

I keep 4 mu in wheat-maize, same as always. That feeds the family. The other 2 mu I put in cotton — it gives us cash for clothes, medicine, and school fees for the grandkids. I've thought about putting more into cotton because the price was decent last year, but cotton needs so much picking labor, and my back isn't what it used to be. Wheat-maize is safer.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th. I buy the common seed from the supply shop in town — about 25 yuan per mu. My neighbor across the lane tried some fancy new variety last year and the stalks lodged bad in the wind, so I'll stick with what I know. Before planting I'll spread about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Costs about 100 yuan a bag now. Then come spring, when the wheat is jointing and if it looks a little yellow, I'll topdress with another 12 kg of urea per mu. All together that's about 10 kg of nitrogen per mu. I know Old Wang down the road puts on more, but last year I did exactly this and got 420 kg per mu, and that's plenty for our flour. More fertilizer means more money upfront, and I need to keep some cash in my pocket in case someone gets sick.

I'll irrigate twice for the wheat — once before winter freeze so the seedlings don't dry out, and once at jointing in March. Pumping water costs about 20 yuan each time per mu, so I don't waste it. If we get a good rain, maybe I skip one, but you can't count on rain around here anymore.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. The window is tight — sometimes only three or four days between cutting wheat and planting maize. I hire a combine for the wheat harvest, 50 yuan per mu, then I plant the maize with my small hand seeder. I put compound fertilizer in the planting holes, about 25 kg per mu, and then topdress with urea when the maize is knee-high, around 15 kg per mu. That gives about 11 kg of nitrogen per mu. If the summer rains come normal, I expect 450 kg per mu. I'll irrigate once or twice depending on how dry July and August get.

For cotton on my 2 mu, I plant in late April after the soil warms up. I plow and make ridges in early April. I put down 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then another 12 kg of urea at flowering time. Cotton needs watching — I spray for bollworm two or three times, and for weeds once. I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. The picking is the hard part, takes all September and October with multiple passes. My daughter-in-law comes back from town to help, thank heavens. If I'm lucky I get 250 kg per mu of seed cotton.

All told, seeds, fertilizer, water, pesticide, and the combine hire will run me about 2,500 yuan this year. That's what I can afford. My son sends some money from town, but I don't like to ask for too much. I'd rather be a little conservative than run out of cash if something goes wrong.
